cf.title: synchronized_standby_slots behavior inconsistent with quorum-based synchronous replication

input.subject: synchronized_standby_slots behavior inconsistent with quorum-based synchronous replication

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and demand for ANY N is shown in messages #1, #2 and #29. Three fixable design points remain at level 2: replication-ondisk-1 (which standby is a safe failover target under ANY), standards-compat-1 (legal slot names that the syncrep scanner may reject) and maintenance-fit-1 (one grammar, two bare-list meanings). The change to the shared syncrep grammar needs sign-off from a committer who knows that code. demand-1 affects only FIRST N.

brief.title: Add ANY N and FIRST N syntax to synchronized_standby_slots
brief.problem: synchronized_standby_slots waits for every listed physical slot, so logical decoding of failover slots stalls when one standby is down. This happens even when synchronous_standby_names uses ANY M quorum commit and the commit is already durable. The author says this also makes WAL pile up on the primary.
brief.proposed_design: The GUC reuses the synchronous_standby_names parser and accepts ANY N (...), FIRST N (...) and N (...); a bare list keeps the old wait-for-all meaning. A first patch adds a SYNC_REP_DEFAULT method to the syncrep parser so a bare list differs from explicit FIRST. ANY skips missing, invalidated and logical slots and counts caught-up ones; FIRST waits on a valid lagging slot rather than skipping to a lower-priority one.
user_visible_surface: synchronized_standby_slots accepts ANY num_sync (slot, ...), FIRST num_sync (...) and num_sync (...); slot names FIRST or ANY need double quotes.
Duplicate slot names are removed silently; num_sync larger than the unique slot count is a GUC check error.
An invalid slot name like 'invalid*' now gives a syntax error from the syncrep parser, not the slot-name error.
New WARNING messages list unusable slots, and a DEBUG1 message reports lagging slots with their restart_lsn.
Docs change for pg_logical_slot_get_changes and pg_replication_slot_advance, which block until the required slots confirm.
author_claims: The default behaviour does not change; a bare list still waits for all slots.
Choosing the right standby at failover is the job of the failover tool, as with quorum synchronous_standby_names.
A reviewer from Fujitsu reports that many customers have asked for this.
The new TAP test runs in about 6 seconds, using a replication connection that holds the slot without advancing it.
brief.thread_state: Several reviewers (shveta malik, Hou zj, Amit Kapila, Dilip Kumar, Shlok Kyal) went through many versions, and on 2026-06-19 shveta called the three-patch set in good shape. No committer has reviewed it, and the last message is from 2026-06-29.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether a committer accepts changing the shared syncrep grammar to add SYNC_REP_DEFAULT.
Ashutosh Sharma's concern that ANY lets the logical subscriber get ahead of a standby that may later be promoted is answered only by pointing to docs.
The proposal does not say how a failover tool finds a promotable standby when slots mix sync and async standbys under ANY.
The proposal does not say whether the changed error for an invalid slot name affects existing configurations or tools.
Dilip Kumar's request to share check-hook code with synchronous_standby_names is left open.

objections.title: Under ANY, which standby the subscriber can safely fail over to changes at runtime
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA sets synchronized_standby_slots = 'ANY 1 (sync_slot, geo_slot)', where geo_slot serves an async standby. The async standby confirms first, so the subscriber applies WAL that the sync standby has not received. The primary then fails, the HA tool promotes the sync standby as quorum commit expects, and the subscriber is now ahead of the new primary and needs a full resync.
objections.argument: Today every slot listed in synchronized_standby_slots is a safe failover target for logical subscribers; under ANY, only the slots that happen to be caught up are safe. Message #5 raised the mixed sync/async case. The answers in messages #4 and #7 leave it to the failover tool, or call such a configuration invalid, but the proposal neither rejects it nor gives tools a way to see which standby is safe. The docs only point to the manual checks in the logical replication failover steps.
objections.author_must_show: How does a failover tool find, from server state alone, which standby holds all WAL already sent to failover-enabled logical subscribers when ANY is in use?

critic.reasoning: Messages #4 and #7 give the task to the failover tool or call the mixed configuration invalid, but the patch cannot reject it and the docs shown do not warn about it. The setting is opt-in, so a documented rule may be enough.

objections.title: Syncrep grammar may reject slot names that are valid today
objections.failure_scenario: A cluster has synchronized_standby_slots = 'first, any' or uses a slot such as '2nd_standby' in postgresql.auto.conf. After an upgrade to the new release, the check hook rejects the value at startup. The DBA finds out when the server will not start, or when the setting is refused during a failover.
objections.argument: Today the value is split with SplitIdentifierString and checked with the slot-name rules, so any legal slot name is accepted. The patch routes the value through the synchronous_standby_names scanner, where FIRST and ANY are keywords and, by the usual identifier rules, a name that starts with a digit likely lexes as NUM followed by NAME. The brief lists only the quoting rule for FIRST and ANY and the changed 'invalid*' error (message #94). The proposal does not list which legal slot names stop parsing, and it does not warn users before upgrade.
objections.author_must_show: Which slot names accepted by the current check hook, such as keywords or names starting with digits, fail under the syncrep scanner, and how are upgraded configurations warned or kept working?

critic.reasoning: Slot names may start with a digit, and the syncrep scanner reads a leading digit run as NUM, so a name like '2nd_standby' would stop parsing unquoted. The thread covers only FIRST, ANY and 'invalid*', and says nothing about existing configurations at upgrade.

objections.title: Shared syncrep grammar now carries two GUCs with different bare-list meanings
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a keyword or a new form to synchronous_standby_names in syncrep_gram.y. synchronized_standby_slots silently accepts the new form, or an existing slot named after the keyword stops parsing, and the server fails to load postgresql.conf after an upgrade. A reviewer of the sync rep patch has no reason to look at slot.c.
objections.argument: Patch 0001 adds SYNC_REP_DEFAULT so one grammar can mean FIRST 1 for one GUC and wait-for-all for the other (messages #26, #74). Every consumer of the parse result must now map DEFAULT correctly, and nothing fails loudly if a new consumer does not. The visible effect has started already: 'invalid*' now gets a parser syntax error, not the slot-name error, and the regression output had to change (message #94). Dilip Kumar's request to share check-hook code between the two GUCs is still open (messages #35, #38), so the two hooks can drift.
objections.author_must_show: What makes a future change to syncrep_gram.y, or a new consumer of SyncRepConfigData, fail a test when it does not handle synchronized_standby_slots and SYNC_REP_DEFAULT?

critic.reasoning: Reviewers weighed the shared-parser cost in messages #31 to #34 and #75, but no committer has accepted it. Nothing in the thread makes a later grammar change fail a test for synchronized_standby_slots, and the check-hook sharing request remains open.

objections.title: No user in the thread asks for FIRST N priority semantics
objections.failure_scenario: A committer takes on patch 0003, which adds a second mode (FIRST N and N (...)) to synchronized_standby_slots, with its own skip and wait rules and its own docs and tests. If no deployment needs priority order for slots, the project maintains and documents that mode for nobody, and its subtle rule of waiting on a valid lagging slot stays untested in the field.
objections.argument: Every demand signal in the thread is about the quorum case: the stall in message #1, WAL growth on the primary in message #2, and customer requests in message #29. Message #64 split the series so that FIRST could be judged on its own merits, but no later message gives a use case for it. Message #71 shows the parser change in 0001 is needed in any case to reject or tell apart explicit FIRST, so a smaller option exists: 0001 plus 0002, with explicit FIRST rejected. Matching the synchronous_standby_names grammar is a reason for consistency, but it does not show that anyone needs the mode.
objections.author_must_show: Which deployment needs logical decoding to wait on the first N slots in priority order, and what would it do if only ANY N were committed?

critic.reasoning: Every demand statement in the thread concerns the quorum case, and no message after the split in #64 gives a use case for FIRST N. Matching the synchronous_standby_names syntax supports consistency but does not show that anyone needs the mode.

refuted.title: Third syncrep_method value changes a struct shared with synchronous_standby_names
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension or monitoring tool reads SyncRepConfig->syncrep_method and handles only PRIORITY and QUORUM. After the change, a bare list in synchronous_standby_names may arrive as SYNC_REP_DEFAULT if any path skips the conversion. The tool then misreports sync_state or picks the wrong candidates.
refuted.argument: Patch 0001 adds SYNC_REP_DEFAULT to the grammar used by synchronous_standby_names, and the synchronous_standby_names side must map it back to PRIORITY with num_sync 1 (message #30). Shveta and the author both doubted that touching the shared parser would be clean (messages #31, #34), and the brief notes that no committer has accepted it. The proposal does not say whether SyncRepConfigData, as seen by synchronous_standby_names, ever carries the new value.
refuted.author_must_show: Does any value of syncrep_method other than PRIORITY or QUORUM reach code or extensions that read synchronous_standby_names, and where is the conversion enforced?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a path that skips the conversion, and the objection names none. SyncRepConfig is built only in the synchronous_standby_names check hook, where message #30 places the mapping to PRIORITY with num_sync 1.

refuted.title: Failover tools can already drop a down standby's slot from the list
refuted.failure_scenario: An HA tool that already rewrites synchronous_standby_names when standby1 dies can also run alter system set synchronized_standby_slots = 'sb2_slot' and reload. Decoding stalls only until the tool reacts. With the patch, users and tools must also learn a second meaning of the syncrep grammar, in which a bare list means all slots.
refuted.argument: The proposal gives the failover tool responsibility for choosing a caught-up standby (messages #4, #6, #8). The same tool can edit synchronized_standby_slots on a reload, so the stall is fixable today, though less conveniently. Messages #1 and #2 describe the indefinite stall and WAL buildup but do not say why reactive reconfiguration is not enough. Demand from customers (message #29) and committer support (message #4) weaken this objection, but they do not answer it.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is changing synchronized_standby_slots from the failover tool when a standby fails not enough, given that the same tool already manages synchronous_standby_names?

critic.reasoning: The thread shows the need is common: message #29 reports requests from many customers, and several independent participants, including a committer in this area, support the idea. The workaround also needs an external tool, and decoding stalls until that tool reacts.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: ANY lets failover-enabled logical decoding proceed before every listed physical standby slot confirms WAL.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: Patch 0001 adds a SYNC_REP_DEFAULT method to the parser result that synchronous_standby_names also uses.

touch_points.label: new GUC
touch_points.reason: No new GUC, but synchronized_standby_slots gets new syntax and FIRST and ANY become keywords in its value.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-1: Syncrep grammar may reject slot names that are valid today

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The syncrep grammar now serves two GUCs whose bare lists mean different things, with separate check hooks.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How does a failover tool find, from server state alone, which standby holds all WAL already sent to failover-enabled logical subscribers when ANY is in use?
Should the docs warn against, or the check hook reject, an ANY list that mixes slots of synchronous and asynchronous standbys?
Which slot names that the current check hook accepts, such as FIRST, ANY or names starting with a digit, fail under the syncrep scanner, and what happens to such configurations at upgrade?
What makes a future change to syncrep_gram.y, or a new reader of the parse result, fail a test when it does not handle synchronized_standby_slots and SYNC_REP_DEFAULT?
Which deployment needs FIRST N for synchronized_standby_slots, and what would it lose if only ANY N were committed and explicit FIRST were rejected?

committability.owner_note: The review notes place Amit Kapila, a committer in this area, in messages #4, #64 and #88, but the brief says no committer has reviewed the patch set. The owner must know slot synchronization and the syncrep parser.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the rule that a logical subscriber never gets ahead of a promotable standby under ANY, and for the shared syncrep grammar serving two GUCs. Both last as long as the syntax exists.
committability.author_follow_up: The author on the CommitFest entry reviewed from message #2 on, and the set went through many versions until June 2026. Nothing is posted after 2026-06-29.

priority.reason: The stall affects sites that combine failover slots with quorum commit, and message #29 reports many customer requests. The three-patch set touches slot.c and the shared syncrep grammar, and a reviewer called it in good shape on 2026-06-19.

provisional_note: Only the first patch's prose was read, and no code. Not checked: whether quoted slot names still pass slot-name validation, which names the scanner rejects, and where SYNC_REP_DEFAULT is mapped for synchronous_standby_names.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronize logical replication slots from primary to standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: A background worker on a physical standby periodically fetches logical replication slot information from the primary, so that after failover a logical subscriber finds up-to-date slots on the new primary. Later versions added synchronize_slot_names on the standby to pick which slots to sync, and standby_slot_names on the primary to hold logical replication back until the listed physical standbys catch up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch breaks the catalog_xmin guarantee: row versions still needed for logical decoding on the standby can be removed. He said it needs a mechanism such as the "Minimal logical decoding on standbys" patch, which the author said was not near ready. Reviewers also objected to the blocking wait and the per-commit work added to reorderbuffer.c, and to the worker-per-database design tied to the logical replication launcher. The author listed these and an open configuration design as significant jobs still to do.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch as-is just breaks one of the fundamental guarantees necessary for logical decoding, that no rows versions can be removed that are still required for logical decoding (signalled via catalog_xmin).

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronizing slots from primary to standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch runs the logical replication launcher on a standby and adds a per-database slotsync worker that periodically fetches slot state from the primary. The worker fast-forwards matching logical slots on the standby, and a new replication command lists the slots on the primary.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread does not record a design objection. The patch depended on the "logical decoding on standby" patch, which was not in the Commitfest, and Thomas Munro reported that the patches no longer applied on top of it. He asked for a rebased patch set, and the shown messages contain no reply from the author before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: You patches no longer apply on top though.

precedents_retrieved.objection: This also requires successful execution of a synchronous notification command.

precedents_retrieved.title: An attempt to avoid locally-committed-but-not-replicated-to-standby-transactions in synchronous replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC, synchronous_replication_naptime_before_cancel, that makes a backend keep waiting for the sync standby ack for a set time before it handles a query cancel or proc die. A second part, not yet coded, would make the primary wait for sync standbys to catch up after a crash restart before it serves the locally committed transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because the patch received no update for six months and no longer applied. The design was still open at the last author message. The author could not reliably detect, at restart, that a backend died while waiting for the sync replication ack, and the alternative of always waiting could keep the primary down. Earlier, Laurenz Albe objected that the approach still left some cases of transactions committed locally but not on the standby.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since there hasn't been any updates for the past six months, and the patch
hasn't applied for a few months, I am marking this returned with feedback for
now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Quorum commit for multiple synchronous replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds quorum commit to synchronous replication through a new 'ANY k (n1, n2, ...)' form of synchronous_standby_names, where the primary waits for acknowledgement from any k of the listed standbys. A later version also adds 'FIRST k (...)' for the existing priority method and makes the bare 'k (...)' form mean quorum.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback at the end of the commitfest because it still needed polishing after his review. His review covered the documentation wording, the case-insensitive flex switch that would make standby names match regardless of case, dead code and unclear comments. The design itself was not rejected, and he invited the author to move it to the next commitfest with a new patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Returned with feedback for now. This just needs polishing so feel free
to move it to the next CF once you have a new patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Minimal logical decoding on standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows logical decoding on a hot standby. It adds a catalog-table flag to existing WAL records so the standby can detect snapshot conflicts with logical slots, and it drops conflicting slots, including when wal_level on the primary drops below logical.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the entry was withdrawn. The last messages show the patch set needing repeated rebases and its TAP tests failing intermittently: Rahila Syed reported 018_standby_logical_decoding_xmins.pl failures, and Alvaro Herrera found 019_standby_logical_decoding_conflicts.pl timing out after a rebase in March 2020. No later reply from the author is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Minimal logical decoding on standbys
precedents_retrieved.authors: Andres Freund (andresfreund), Craig Ringer (ringerc), Amit Khandekar (amitdkhan), Ibrar Ahmed (ibrar)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows logical decoding on a physical standby, with catalog-row conflicts on the standby detected from the existing snapshot-conflict WAL records, which gain a flag marking catalog tables. It replaces an earlier design that periodically logged the primary's catalog xmin horizon, and leaves hot_standby_feedback optional.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry died of inactivity. In March 2020 Alvaro Herrera rebased the patch, and its new conflict test then timed out and stopped the test run. No updated version followed, so after six months without updates Michael Paquier returned it with feedback, noting that the patch no longer applied.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
No updates in the last six months, so I am marking it as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronous replay mode for avoiding stale reads on hot standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a synchronous_replay mode in which a commit on the primary waits until all available hot standbys have replayed it, and the primary grants time-limited leases to standbys. A standby without a valid lease rejects synchronous_replay transactions with a new error 40P02, so reads on standbys never miss a commit that has already returned on the primary.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message, from February 2019, is a rebase by the author, and the entry was withdrawn in July 2019. Open items still visible at that point included missing TAP tests, an unexplained replication protocol corruption bug, and design questions from Masahiko Sawada about the GUCs.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P6] added ANY/FIRST to synchronous_standby_names and was returned only for polishing, [P1] died on catalog_xmin safety in slot sync, and [P12] records no reason, so none of their reasons applies here. Messages #4 and #6 point to an earlier thread where the same idea came up; they report only that the approach was similar and that it included a default-to-synchronous_standby_names option, which messages #10 to #12 then dropped.

Other compatibility points look settled in the thread. These include the bare-list default, removing duplicates, the error when N is larger than the number of unique slots, and the updated function docs.

The proposal adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog or wire protocol change. Its only persistent effect is the GUC value, and a bare list keeps today's wait-for-all meaning, so the replication concern above is the only one this angle finds.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. synchronized_standby_slots stays a server-level setting that only superusers or ALTER SYSTEM can change, and logical decoding still needs REPLICATION or a slot owner. The new WARNING and DEBUG1 messages show slot names and restart_lsn values, which pg_replication_slots already shows. A single setting bounds the per-check state, so it adds no new denial-of-service path. One point cannot be checked without the code: whether quoted members still pass slot-name validation, and that is a correctness question.

Other maintenance points do not hold. Amit Kapila is engaged as a committer in this area (messages #4, #64, #88). Costs fall mainly on users who set the new syntax. No external dependency is added. The patch set is split into separately reviewable steps.
No extension or contrib module offers this. The patch reuses the existing syncrep parser, so it does not add a second mechanism.

Demand for the ANY N part is real. It rests on a concrete stall scenario under quorum commit (message #1), reports of WAL growth on the primary (message #2), a Fujitsu reviewer citing many customer requests (message #29), and reviewers from several companies, so the only objection here concerns FIRST N.

warnings: synthesis said NEEDS-COMMITTER-EYES but listed a level 1b objection (demand-1); changed to NEEDS-DESIGN-DISCUSSION
